commits.message:
[ssbuffer](feat) Add pattern for scalar bound path (#3348)

* [ssbuffer](feat) add pattern for scalar bound

* [ssbuffer](feat) add pattern for short chain

The hstu attention pipeline is a chain of three computation blocks that
alternates the cores: cube block 4 -> vector block 11 -> cube block 6. It
holds two transfers, so it carries four tightly coupled buffers. The blocks
that carry a condition are the three blocks of the chain and one more block
that takes part in no cross core transfer, so the kernel holds four of them.

The shape is recognized on three conditions, so that no other kernel matches
it by accident: the chain has to be a linear chain, every transfer has to
carry two tightly coupled buffers and the chain has to carry four buffers of
its own, and the kernel has to hold exactly four blocks that carry a
condition, three of them cross core.

 namespace mlir {
 namespace triton {
 
+/// The shape of the cross-core dependency graph of the blocks that carry a
+/// condition.
+enum class CrossCoreShape {
+  /// The graph does not hold a shape the normal preload scheme models.
+  None,
+  /// A linear chain of four or five blocks: the mla and paged decode
+  /// pipelines.
+  LinearChain,
+  /// Two linear chains of four blocks sharing no block and no buffer.
+  TwoChains,
+  /// A linear chain of three blocks: the hstu attention pipeline.
+  ShortChain,
+  /// A tree of six or seven blocks that may fork and merge: the nsa
+  /// compression backward pipeline.
+  Tree,
+  /// A forest of four chains of three blocks sharing no block and no
+  /// buffer: the flex attention backward pipeline.
+  ShortChainForest,
+};
+
 /// The shape of the cross-core dependency graph of a module.
 struct CrossCorePattern {
   /// The number of independent pipelines of the graph.
   unsigned pipelines = 0;
-  /// The number of entry blocks of the pipelines: the blocks of the
-  /// qualifying chains that no other block of the chains feeds. A pipeline
-  /// that is a single linear chain has one entry; two blocks feeding the
-  /// same block is a merge, and the merge has two entries.
+  /// The number of entry blocks of the pipelines: the blocks that no other
+  /// block of the chains feeds. A merge has two entries.
   unsigned entries = 0;
+  /// The shape the graph holds.
+  CrossCoreShape shape = CrossCoreShape::None;
 };
 
 /// Analyzes the cross-core dependency graph of `module` and reports its
 /// pipelines.
-///
-/// The nodes of the graph are the computation blocks, a block being the pair
-/// of the scope that holds it and its `ssbuffer.block_id`; block ids are only
-/// unique inside a scope. The edges are the cross-core dependencies, the
-/// producer block of a dependency group feeding the consumer block of the
-/// same group. Every edge joins two different cores, so a chain always
-/// alternates the cores: CUBE -> VECTOR -> CUBE -> VECTOR or VECTOR -> CUBE
-/// -> VECTOR -> CUBE.
-///
-/// A chain has to carry the tightly coupled buffers of the validated
-/// pipeline: every transfer of the chain is double buffered and no buffer is
-/// shared by two transfers of the chain, so the chain of `chainLength` blocks
-/// uses 2 * (chainLength - 1) tightly coupled buffers.
-///
-/// One direction of the graph may be carried by several cross-core groups.
-/// The buffers of the direction are the buffers of all of them, and the
-/// direction has to carry the buffers of exactly one transfer, so that every
-/// transfer of the pipeline carries the same number of buffers.
-///
-/// The conditions are computed for the blocks that carry a condition, so the
-/// cross-core blocks of the module that carry a condition have to be the
-/// blocks of one of the two validated pipelines: four of them for the mla
-/// pipeline and five of them for the paged decode pipeline.
-///
-/// Two chains that share a block are two views of the same pipeline and count
-/// once; the chains that share no block are independent pipelines.
 CrossCorePattern analyzeCrossCorePattern(ModuleOp module,
                                          unsigned chainLength = 4);

+// A kernel whose pipeline is a forest of four chains of three computation

+//   cube 5 -> vector 24 -> cube 7
+//   cube 9 -> vector 25 -> cube 11
+//   cube 13 -> vector 27 -> cube 15

+# Paged MLA with explicit L0 scheduling
+
+BF16 packed Q and KV, causal paged attention, FP32 online softmax, and BF16
+output with FP32 LSE. The tuned kernel stages QK and PV through L0 and fuses
+the split merge when its workspace fits. The tests cover the full context and
+ragged page tables.
+
+Run from the repository root:
+
+```sh
+suite=third_party/ascend/unittest/tla_ut/kernels/mla
+TLA_TEST_STAGE=ir python -m pytest -q "$suite"
+TLA_TEST_STAGE=run python -m pytest -q "$suite" -k test_run
+TLA_TEST_STAGE=run TLA_RUN_PERF=1 python -m pytest -s "$suite" -k test_perf
+```
+
+Historical device median on Ascend 950PR with CANN 9.1.0, B=8, H=24,
+Sq=4, Skv=143360, QK=576, V=512 and page size 128:
+
+| Implementation | Device median |
+| --- | ---: |
+| TLA explicit L0 | 818.277 µs |
+| Source-built Ascend C | 824.594 µs |
+| CANNBot DSL | 861.277 µs |
+
+Timing sums every device task in an invocation, including the merge when
+separate. The benchmark checks the FP32 reference before profiling.
+
+On Triton Ascend `3cc904692` with AscendNPU-IR `0167d41d` and CANN 9.1.0,
+the full and ragged cases passed IR and accuracy checks. The full case
+measured 830.7 µs device time and 878.7 µs synchronized wall time
+(three rounds of 40 device samples).

+"""FP32 reference and inputs for paged MLA examples."""
+
+import torch
+
+
+def make_inputs(lengths, family, seed):
+    """Use random physical pages, including unused slots in shorter requests."""
+    generator = torch.Generator(device='cpu').manual_seed(seed)
+    page_counts = [(length + 127) // 128 for length in lengths]
+    ids = torch.randperm(sum(page_counts), generator=generator, dtype=torch.int32)
+    table = torch.full((len(lengths), max(page_counts)), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    for row, pages in enumerate(ids.split(page_counts)):
+        table[row, :pages.numel()] = pages
+    device = torch.device('npu', torch.npu.current_device())
+
+    def random(shape, query=False):
+        if query and family == 'uniform':
+            return torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+        data = torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=generator)
+        if query and family == 'peaked':
+            data.mul_(8)
+        return data.to(device)
+
+    # Retain the input generation order of the pre-cleanup benchmark.
+    q = random((len(lengths), 4, 24, 512), query=True)
+    qr = random((len(lengths), 4, 24, 64), query=True)
+    kv = random((ids.numel(), 128, 512))
+    kr = random((ids.numel(), 128, 64))
+    packed_q = torch.cat((q, qr), dim=-1)
+    packed_kv = torch.cat((kv, kr), dim=-1)
+    return packed_q, packed_kv, table.to(device), torch.tensor(lengths, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+
+
+def reference(inputs):
+    """Independent FP32 attention with one full softmax per query row."""
+    q, kv, table, lengths = inputs
+    batch, sq, heads, _ = q.shape
+    table_cpu, lengths_cpu = table.cpu(), lengths.cpu().tolist()
+    outputs, lses = [], []
+    for request, length in enumerate(lengths_cpu):
+        pages = table_cpu[request, :(length + 127) // 128].to(q.device, torch.int64)
+        keys = kv.index_select(0, pages).reshape(-1, 576)[:length].float()
+        query = q[request].reshape(-1, 576).float()
+        positions = torch.arange(length, device=q.device)
+        visible_end = length - sq + torch.arange(sq, device=q.device).repeat_interleave(heads)
+        values, normalizers = [], []
+        for start in range(0, sq * heads, 16):
+            rows = slice(start, start + 16)
+            logits = (query[rows, :512] @ keys[:, :512].T + query[rows, 512:] @ keys[:, 512:].T) * 0.04
+            logits.masked_fill_(positions[None, :] > visible_end[rows, None], -float('inf'))
+            values.append(logits.softmax(-1) @ keys[:, :512])
+            normalizers.append(logits.logsumexp(-1))
+        outputs.append(torch.cat(values).reshape(sq, heads, 512))
+        lses.append(torch.cat(normalizers).reshape(sq, heads))
+    return torch.stack(outputs), torch.stack(lses)
+
+
+def precision(call, expected):
+    actual = call()
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+    assert isinstance(actual, tuple) and len(actual) == 2, 'Expected both output and LSE'
+    result = {}
+    for name, output, target, dtype, tolerance in zip(('output', 'lse'), actual, expected,
+                                                      (torch.bfloat16, torch.float32), (0.005, 0.0001)):
+        assert output.shape == target.shape and output.dtype == dtype, name
+        assert torch.isfinite(output).all(), name
+        error = output.float() - target
+        maximum = (error.abs().amax() / target.abs().amax().clamp_min(1e-30)).item()
+        rms = (error.square().mean().sqrt() / target.square().mean().sqrt().clamp_min(1e-30)).item()
+        assert maximum <= tolerance and rms <= tolerance, (name, maximum, rms)
+        result[name] = dict(normalized_max_error=maximum, relative_rms=rms)
+    return result
